text: I’ll model the wing with chord along \(x\), span along \(+y\), and thickness/camber along \(z\). The root lies on the \(y=0\) wall. I’ll use a half-domain bounded by that wall: \(x=-0.48\) to \(1.08\) m, \(y=0\) to \(0.56\) m, and \(z=-0.36\) to \(0.36\) m. Here “3 chords to each side and above” is interpreted as three root chords above/below and beyond the tip. I’ll create the exact NACA sections and subtract their loft from this box; first I’m checking the installed CAD API needed for that construction.
The installed version does not expose `make_polygon`; I’ll query the available algebra-mode wire and loft constructors before creating the solid.

The constructors are available. I’ll now build the ruled loft from two closed NACA 2412 wires, subtract it from the domain box, print the requested chord/span measurements, and render the coarse CAD before creating any mesh.

The coarse preview shows the intended unswept, untwisted tapered wing in the half-domain. The small chord measurement excess (10 µm at root) is the standard NACA 4-digit coordinate convention, where the camber-line angle shifts the nominal trailing-edge point slightly aft; I’ll retain the standard profile. Next I’ll trace the Boolean-result faces back to the explicitly created box and wing faces, so patch names come from their source surfaces rather than from bounding-box position.

Face provenance is clean: five box faces survive unchanged, 162 wing faces survive unchanged, and the only modified face is the \(y=0\) root wall with the attached airfoil footprint removed. I’ll use those source relationships to form the five requested patches and export them together so shared STL edges are tessellated consistently.

The patch partition covers every face exactly, but this helper version does not accept an output-directory argument. I’ll query its installed signature and then call it from the target directory as required.
I’ll repeat the deterministic provenance partition in an accepted cell and export to the helper’s default `constant/triSurface` path.

The exported union is watertight and consistently wound. For the first mesh I’ll use a structured 20 mm background grid (about 79,000 cells) with the outer patch names created directly in `blockMesh`, then `snappyHexMesh` will cut the wing and refine its surface by two levels to about 5 mm. This is deliberately coarse enough to inspect quickly; the wing STL is used only for the immersed wing because the outer STL surfaces coincide with the already named block boundaries.
I’ll generate the background mesh first and verify its patch topology before cutting the wing.
The background grid is exactly 20 mm and has the four outer patch groups. I’ll now cut and snap the wing at two refinement levels.

`snappyHexMesh` requires placeholder numerical dictionaries even though no solver will be run. I’ll add only those mandatory mesh-utility files, without defining any boundary conditions or solution setup.
I’ll rerun the wing cutting now that the mesh utility’s required dictionaries exist.
The coarse snapped mesh completed with 85,305 cells and no mesher quality errors. I’ll run the binding `checkMesh` now and inspect patch counts.

`checkMesh` passes: one region, five patches, 85,305 cells, maximum non-orthogonality \(42.0^\circ\), maximum skewness 1.64. I’ll render the final volume mesh with a cutaway and highlighted wing to visually confirm the removed airfoil and root attachment.
The VTK export contains all five named boundaries. I’ll inspect a mid-span mesh slice together with the full wing surface.

The final inspection shows the refined cutout around the wing, the tip surface, and the root attachment to the wall. The mesh is complete: 85,305 cells, five named boundary patches, and one STL per requested patch. The only modeling assumption was the interpretation of the domain wording as a root-wall half-domain with three root chords below/above and beyond the tip; downstream distance is measured from the root trailing edge. The standard NACA coordinate formula yields geometric extents 0.120010 m and 0.080007 m versus nominal 0.120 m and 0.080 m chords; span is exactly 0.200 m. No requested property remains unchecked.

The advisory coverage check confirms all 656 triangles are assigned to exactly one of the five patches; its warning is informational rather than a geometry defect, so I am explicitly waiving it on that basis.
